newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London finished mixed but well above session lows. November lost $19 to close at $1,463, while January shed $2 to close at $1,385. Friday is the first notice-tender day for November and the spread could come under further pressure as more coffee is delivered against the spot month.

In New York arabica futures ended mixed with the spot December contract losing ground on fund selling and liquidation of the nearby switch. The December was hit the hardest, with rolling of speculative longs out of December and to second-month March ahead of the start of the month-long delivery period November 19. However, nearby supplies are expected to remain tight possibly up to the end of the year.

Traders said roasters are running out of coffee and are willing to pay substantial premiums. With European spot inventories also running low, traders said US roasters were not only fighting internally for coffee but bidding against European roaster too. Although Colombian coffee is expected to begin flowing into the market following the end of the truckers' strike it will be likely to be mid-November before deliveries get back to normal.

CANADA - Canada imported 228,102 bags of coffee in June 1996, 14 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.367 million bags, nearly 13 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell by 11 per cent to 2.510 million bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Guatemala (143,700 vs 100,200 bags), Mexico (173,300 vs 80,100 bags) and Colombia (225,800 vs 177,300 bags).

The country exported 161,400 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 1.4 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 fell to 303,800 bags from 334,400 bags the previous year.

NEW ZEALAND - New Zealand imported 124,400 bags of coffee in January/September 1996 and nearly 12 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose slightly by 1 per cent to 149,500 bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Indonesia (27,300 vs 27,500 bags), Vietnam (20,600 vs 20,100 bags) and Papua New Guinea (19,500 vs 17,100 bags). Australia shipped 18,900 bags of solubles to New Zealand in January/September 1996 which compares to 16,500 bags the same period in 1995.
